variants.title: Follow the teacher-to-student path
variants.context: Distillation runs from a qualified teacher to an independently released student: qualify the teacher, build transfer examples, train the student on both signals, then release on the student's own measured evidence.
variants.prompt: A team wants a cheaper classifier for an existing production model. Put the distillation stages in order.

items.text: Train the student: combine ground-truth loss with teacher outputs or compatible intermediate features.
Release independently: benchmark the exported student on target hardware and block promotion when a gate fails.
Qualify the teacher: freeze a version whose task quality, calibration, failure slices, and data lineage are understood.
Build transfer examples: gather representative, permitted inputs covering the workload the student must handle.

variants.hint: The student is released on its own evidence, not on how closely it tracked the teacher.
variants.explanation: Distillation changes training only, so the deployed student must still satisfy its own quality, slice, latency, memory, and cost contract.

variants.title: Follow the teacher-to-student path
variants.context: Distillation runs from a qualified teacher to an independently released student: qualify the teacher, build transfer examples, train the student on both signals, then release on the student's own measured evidence.
variants.prompt: The teacher is upgraded to a newer checkpoint with different preprocessing. Put the stages in order for the rebuild.

items.text: Train the student: rerun training with the refreshed signals and the same ground-truth anchor.
Build transfer examples: recompute teacher outputs, since the cached signals were produced under the old preprocessing contract.
Qualify the teacher: re-examine the new checkpoint's quality, calibration, and failure slices before trusting its outputs.
Release independently: rebenchmark the exported student rather than reusing the previous release evidence.

variants.hint: Cached teacher outputs are tied to the artifact and preprocessing that produced them.
variants.explanation: Every cached signal carries the teacher artifact and preprocessing version, so a teacher change invalidates the cache and every downstream result.

variants.title: Follow the teacher-to-student path
variants.context: Distillation runs from a qualified teacher to an independently released student: qualify the teacher, build transfer examples, train the student on both signals, then release on the student's own measured evidence.
variants.prompt: A student must serve a new language the teacher already handles. Put the stages in order.

items.text: Train the student: train on the extended transfer set with labels still anchoring the objective.
Release independently: gate the new language slice on the student's measured quality and target-device cost.
Build transfer examples: add permitted inputs in the new language so the teacher actually produces signal there.
Qualify the teacher: confirm the teacher's own quality and failure slices in that language before copying its behavior.

variants.hint: What the teacher never sees on the transfer inputs cannot reach the student.
variants.explanation: The transfer set bounds what can be distilled, so a new population needs teacher signal on that population and its own release slice.

variants.title: Compute one distillation step
variants.context: One response-distillation step has a fixed order. The frozen teacher runs without gradients, both logit sets are softened by temperature, the student branch enters KL in log space, the soft term is scaled by T squared, and then the losses blend.
variants.prompt: A PyTorch training step blends teacher and label signals. Put the operations in order.

items.text: Compute the KL with batchmean reduction and multiply the result by T squared.
Take log_softmax of the temperature-scaled student logits, because KLDivLoss expects its input in log space.
Blend the scaled soft loss with the label loss using the declared teacher weight, then return detached metrics.
Run the frozen teacher in evaluation mode under no_grad to obtain teacher logits.
Divide the teacher logits by the temperature and softmax them into the soft targets.

variants.hint: One branch of the loss must be in log space and the other in probability space.
variants.explanation: The teacher stays frozen, the student branch enters KL as log probabilities, and the T squared factor keeps the gradient scale comparable across temperatures.

variants.title: Compute one distillation step
variants.context: One response-distillation step has a fixed order. The frozen teacher runs without gradients, both logit sets are softened by temperature, the student branch enters KL in log space, the soft term is scaled by T squared, and then the losses blend.
variants.prompt: Teacher logits were precomputed and cached to cut training cost. Put the operations of the step in order.

items.text: Divide the cached logits by the temperature and softmax them into the soft targets.
Take log_softmax of the temperature-scaled student logits for the KL input.
Blend with the label loss under the declared teacher weight so ground truth still anchors the update.
Load the cached teacher logits keyed to the teacher artifact, preprocessing version, and label mapping.
Compute the KL with batchmean reduction and apply the T squared factor.

variants.hint: Caching replaces one operation and leaves the rest of the order untouched.
variants.explanation: Cached logits make training cheaper and reproducible, but the softening, log-space input, T squared scaling, and label anchor are unchanged.

variants.title: Compute one distillation step
variants.context: One response-distillation step has a fixed order. The frozen teacher runs without gradients, both logit sets are softened by temperature, the student branch enters KL in log space, the soft term is scaled by T squared, and then the losses blend.
variants.prompt: A student's loss collapses to near zero and gradients look wrong. Put the correct operations in order to audit the step.

items.text: Confirm the reduction was batchmean and that the T squared factor was applied once.
Confirm the teacher ran under no_grad in evaluation mode so no gradient flows back into it.
Confirm the label loss still contributes through its own weight in the blend.
Confirm both logit sets were divided by the same temperature before any softmax.
Confirm the student entered KL as log probabilities rather than as probabilities.

variants.hint: Audit the step in the order the values are produced.
variants.explanation: Most distillation defects are order or contract errors, so the step is checked from the teacher forward pass through to the blend.

variants.title: Blend the two losses
variants.context: The objective is total_loss = teacher_weight times soft_loss plus (1 - teacher_weight) times label_loss. The soft term is the KL between softened distributions multiplied by T squared so its gradient scale stays comparable across temperatures.
variants.prompt: A batch gives a raw soft KL of 0.05 at temperature 4, a label loss of 1.6, and a teacher weight of 0.5. What is the total loss?
variants.hint: Scale the soft term before it is weighted.
variants.explanation: The soft term becomes 0.05 times 16, which is 0.8, and the blend gives 0.5 times 0.8 plus 0.5 times 1.6, so the total is 1.2.

mistakes.feedback: That skips the T squared factor, so the soft term contributes almost nothing to the update.
That multiplies by T instead of T squared, which is the wrong gradient scaling for the soft branch.

variants.title: Blend the two losses
variants.context: The objective is total_loss = teacher_weight times soft_loss plus (1 - teacher_weight) times label_loss. The soft term is the KL between softened distributions multiplied by T squared so its gradient scale stays comparable across temperatures.
variants.prompt: A batch gives a raw soft KL of 0.2 at temperature 3, a label loss of 1.0, and a teacher weight of 0.75. What is the total loss?
variants.hint: Apply the temperature convention first, then the declared weights.
variants.explanation: The soft term becomes 0.2 times 9, which is 1.8, and the blend gives 0.75 times 1.8 plus 0.25 times 1.0, so the total is 1.6.

mistakes.feedback: That omits the T squared factor, leaving the teacher signal far smaller than the objective intends.
That scales by T rather than T squared, so the soft branch is understated at this temperature.

variants.title: Blend the two losses
variants.context: The objective is total_loss = teacher_weight times soft_loss plus (1 - teacher_weight) times label_loss. The soft term is the KL between softened distributions multiplied by T squared so its gradient scale stays comparable across temperatures.
variants.prompt: A cautious recipe uses a teacher weight of 0.25 with a raw soft KL of 0.3 at temperature 2 and a label loss of 0.4. What is the total loss?
variants.hint: The complement of the teacher weight is what the labels receive.
variants.explanation: The soft term becomes 0.3 times 4, which is 1.2, and the blend gives 0.25 times 1.2 plus 0.75 times 0.4, so the total is 0.6.

mistakes.feedback: That leaves out the T squared factor before weighting the soft term.
That swaps the weights, giving the teacher 0.75 and the labels 0.25.

variants.title: Diagnose the student
variants.context: Matching the teacher during training is evidence, not a production guarantee. Distillation cannot transfer behavior the teacher never produced on the transfer inputs, and parameter count does not decide latency or memory.
variants.prompt: A student matches the teacher's distribution closely on the transfer set, but on a support cohort that speaks a language absent from the transfer inputs its answers are unusable. What is the finding?
options: The transfer set never covered that cohort, so no teacher behavior for it was ever available to distill.
The teacher weight is too low, so the student fell back on noisy labels for the underrepresented cohort.
The student lacks capacity for that cohort, so the architecture needs more parameters before retraining.
optionFeedback: Correct: distillation cannot transfer behavior the teacher never produced on the transfer inputs.
Reweighting cannot conjure a teacher signal for inputs the teacher was never run on.
Capacity is a plausible cause elsewhere, but here the cohort has no training signal of either kind.
variants.hint: Ask what the teacher was actually asked about.
variants.explanation: The transfer set bounds what can be transferred, so coverage of cohorts, languages, and lengths is checked before any objective is tuned.

variants.title: Diagnose the student
variants.context: Matching the teacher during training is evidence, not a production guarantee. Distillation cannot transfer behavior the teacher never produced on the transfer inputs, and parameter count does not decide latency or memory.
variants.prompt: On a slice where the teacher is known to be wrong, the student now reproduces the teacher's error and ignores the correct label. The recipe uses a teacher weight of 0.9. What should the team do?
options: Raise the temperature so the teacher distribution softens and its confident mistake carries less weight.
Remove the label loss entirely and retrain on teacher outputs so the objective stops fighting itself.
Lower the teacher weight so ground truth anchors the update, and inspect the disagreement slice directly.
optionFeedback: Softening spreads probability mass but leaves the teacher's ranking, so the same wrong answer still dominates.
Dropping ground truth removes the only signal that can contradict the teacher on this slice.
Correct: a high teacher weight pulls the student toward a wrong prediction, and the label anchor is what prevents it.
variants.hint: Which signal in the objective can disagree with the teacher?
variants.explanation: Hard targets exist because a teacher can be uncertain, biased, stale, or wrong, so disagreement slices are inspected and the label anchor preserved.

variants.title: Diagnose the student
variants.context: Matching the teacher during training is evidence, not a production guarantee. Distillation cannot transfer behavior the teacher never produced on the transfer inputs, and parameter count does not decide latency or memory.
variants.prompt: A student has one eighth of the teacher's parameters and its file is far smaller, but measured p95 latency on the serving device is unchanged. What is the defensible conclusion?
options: The student is underfitting, so its extra work comes from longer output sequences during generation.
Parameter count did not decide latency here, so the exported artifact must be profiled in its actual runtime.
The benchmark harness is at fault, since a model with one eighth the parameters cannot take the same time.
optionFeedback: Underfitting is a quality symptom and does not by itself explain unchanged latency percentiles.
Correct: kernel support, sequence shape, batching, preprocessing, and data movement all affect end-to-end latency.
Assuming the harness is wrong because the ratio is surprising skips the measurement that would settle it.
variants.hint: Which of these numbers was measured on the serving device?
variants.explanation: Parameter count and artifact size are inventory fields, so latency and memory claims require benchmarking the exported artifact on target hardware.

variants.title: Map each part to its job
variants.context: Distillation has named parts with separate jobs: the four moving pieces of the objective, the transfer signals the architectures can support, and the failure modes that each call for a different fix.
variants.prompt: Match each moving part of distillation to its role.

pairs.label: Teacher
pairs.detail: A trained model kept in evaluation mode that produces the behavior to transfer and receives no gradients.

pairs.label: Student
pairs.detail: A separately parameterized deployment candidate that receives the gradients and serves requests alone.

pairs.label: Soft targets
pairs.detail: A distribution from teacher logits that exposes relative preferences across classes.

pairs.label: Hard targets
pairs.detail: Labels or task outcomes that anchor training to observed truth when the teacher is wrong.

variants.hint: Two parts supply signal and two parts decide what learns from it.
variants.explanation: Naming the four parts is what keeps a training-time signal from being confused with a production guarantee.

variants.title: Map each part to its job
variants.context: Distillation has named parts with separate jobs: the four moving pieces of the objective, the transfer signals the architectures can support, and the failure modes that each call for a different fix.
variants.prompt: Match each transfer signal to what the architectures must support for it.

pairs.label: Response distillation
pairs.detail: Aligned output dimensions on the same task, matching output distributions directly.

pairs.label: Feature distillation
pairs.detail: An explicit projection or pooling rule when hidden shapes differ, plus a validated layer pairing.

pairs.label: Relational distillation
pairs.detail: Transfer of pairwise distances, attention maps, or similarity structure rather than component equality.

variants.hint: Ask what has to line up between the two networks for the signal to be defined at all.
variants.explanation: No signal is automatically superior, and feature or attention matching adds memory and architecture coupling that must earn its place on holdout evidence.

variants.title: Map each part to its job
variants.context: Distillation has named parts with separate jobs: the four moving pieces of the objective, the transfer signals the architectures can support, and the failure modes that each call for a different fix.
variants.prompt: Match each distillation failure to the diagnosis it points to.

pairs.label: Student copies a teacher error
pairs.detail: Teacher and label disagreement under a high teacher weight.

pairs.label: Soft targets look like one-hot labels
pairs.detail: Outputs too sharp for the chosen temperature to expose class structure.

pairs.label: Student cannot fit the teacher anywhere
pairs.detail: A capacity gap or structural mismatch in the student architecture.

pairs.label: Average holds while one slice drops
pairs.detail: Aggregate-only evaluation hiding a concentrated regression.

variants.hint: Each symptom has a different fix, so name the symptom before changing the recipe.
variants.explanation: Diagnosing the specific failure prevents adding feature or attention objectives that increase cost without improving the deployed student.
